docs.title: LakeLogic MCP
docs.text:
Help AI assistants check and test data contracts locally.

Validate Open Lakehouse Contracts (OLC), find governance gaps, explain rules and generate sample data. Test-run contracts with LakeLogic Core using Polars or DuckDB, then inspect accepted rows, failed rows and the reasons they failed.

Works with MCP-compatible assistants — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and others. No LakeLogic account required.

OLC defines the contract. Core executes it. MCP gives your assistant access to those tools.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
"Check orders.yaml, explain any findings, generate sample data and test it locally."

The assistant validates the contract, lints it, explains each finding, writes test data shaped by the contract, runs it, and reports which rows passed and why the others failed — real results from LakeLogic, not plausible-looking YAML.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text: Ask Tool Does it match the OLC model? validate_contract Does it pass the lint checks? lint_contract Why is this rule flagged? explain_rule How is this part of a contract written? contract_reference Give me the ODCS version export_odcs Make me test data for it generate_test_data What happens when it runs? run_contract

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
claude mcp add lakelogic -- uvx lakelogic-mcp

Start your assistant in the project that holds your contracts. Other clients: see Install. Before running contracts on real data, read Safety and privacy.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Work on the server from a checkout, next to checkouts of open-lakehouse-contract and LakeLogic.

cd lakelogic-mcp
uv venv .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python "mcp>=1.2" pytest -e ../open-lakehouse-contract -e ../lakelogic
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e .
.venv/bin/python -m pytest

On Windows use .venv\Scripts\python.exe.

docs.title: Use your checkout in Claude Code
docs.text:
From the project whose contracts you want checked:

claude mcp add lakelogic -- /path/to/lakelogic-mcp/.venv/bin/lakelogic-mcp

docs.title: The docs
docs.text:
This site is built with Material for MkDocs and published to GitHub Pages on every push to main.

pip install -r docs-requirements.txt
mkdocs serve      # http://127.0.0.1:8012

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Every client starts the server with uv, so uv must be on your PATH. The server works on the folder it is started in: start your client from the project that holds your contracts, or pass --root.

Claude CodeCursorClaude Desktop, VS Code and others

As a plugin:

/plugin marketplace add LakeLogic/lakelogic-mcp
/plugin install lakelogic-mcp@lakelogic-mcp

Or directly:

claude mcp add lakelogic -- uvx lakelogic-mcp

Add to Cursor

Or add it to Cursor's mcp.json as below.

Add to the client's MCP settings (claude_desktop_config.json, mcp.json, …):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lakelogic": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["lakelogic-mcp", "--root", "/path/to/your/contracts/project"]
    }
  }
}

It is also listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.LakeLogic/lakelogic-mcp.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Meaning --root <folder> The project folder the tools may read and write. Default: the folder the server starts in. LAKELOGIC_MCP_ROOT The same, as an environment variable.

docs.title: Check it works
docs.text: Ask your assistant: "List the LakeLogic tools you have." It should name the seven tools on the Tools page. Then: "Validate the contracts in this folder."

docs.title: Safety and privacy
docs.text: An assistant with tools can do things. This page says what these tools do, and where the limits are.

docs.title: The server
docs.text:
• Local. It talks to your MCP client over stdio. The server itself opens no network connection, needs no account and sends no telemetry. (Installing it with uvx downloads the package and its dependencies, like any install.)
  • Tool paths stay in your project. Every path given to a tool is resolved inside the folder the server was started in (or --root). A path that points outside it — including through .. — is refused. The _domain.yaml / _system.yaml that lint_contract takes into account are searched for only inside the project too.

docs.title: When a contract runs
docs.text:
run_contract hands the contract to LakeLogic Core, which does what the contract configures. Two things follow:

  • A contract can configure network calls. If it declares notifications (for example a Slack webhook) or run-log delivery to a service, Core may send them during the run. Run contracts you trust, or remove those blocks before a test run.
  • A contract can point at other files. Files the contract itself names — a reference dataset under links:, for example — are read by Core and are not limited to the project folder.

Nothing is written to the contract's target table either way.

docs.title: What the two local tools write
docs.text:
Tool Writes Where generate_test_data A synthetic data file test_data/ (or the output you give), inside the project run_contract Nothing, unless write_outputs is set; then the good and quarantined rows runs/, inside the project

Both are marked to the client as not read-only, so most clients ask before running them. The five other tools are marked read-only.

docs.title: What reaches your AI provider
docs.text: Running locally does not keep results away from the assistant. Every tool result goes into the assistant's context, and so to whichever model provider your client uses. run_contract returns counts, failure reasons and a sample of rows (sample, default 10). If a data file holds real personal data, test with generated data instead, or set sample to 0.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Seven tools. Five only read a contract and report; two act locally — one writes a test-data file, one runs a contract on a local file. Clients may call the read-only tools without asking each time (they are marked read-only to the client); the other two ask first in most clients.

Paths are files inside the project the server was started in. Every tool returns a JSON object; a problem comes back as {"error": "..."}, never a crash.

The server also tells the assistant how to use them together: after writing or changing a contract, validate, then lint, and fix what they report before showing it.

docs.title: validate_contract
docs.text:
Does it match the OLC model? Known keys, the right shapes, required fields.

Input path A contract file in the project contract_yaml Or the contract's text

Returns valid and, if not, each error's location and problem.

docs.title: lint_contract
docs.text:
Does it pass the lint checks? Governance gaps such as a merge with no key, unordered deduplication, untagged personal data, or a step no engine runs. Use after validate_contract passes.

Input path A contract file in the project contract_yaml Or the contract's text

Returns clean and findings, each with its rule code, severity and fix.

docs.title: explain_rule
docs.text:
Why does a lint rule exist? What it checks, why it matters, a failing contract and the fixed one.

Input code A lint rule code, e.g. KEY-002

docs.title: contract_reference
docs.text:
How is one part of a contract written? Returns the OLC reference page for that part.

Input topic One of: anatomy (every key), execution-order, ingestion, lifecycle, quality, security, compliance, transformation, external-logic, materialization, server, lineage, data-products, slo, notifications, extraction, conformance, cli, schema

docs.title: export_odcs
docs.text:
The contract as an Open Data Contract Standard document.

Input path A contract file in the project

docs.title: generate_test_data
docs.text:
Synthetic data shaped by the contract — the right types, accepted values and ranges — with a share of rows that deliberately break its quality rules, so a run shows quarantine working. Writes a file in the project.

Input Default path The contract file rows 100 How many rows invalid_ratio 0.1 Share of rows that break a rule seed random For repeatable data output test_data/<contract>.csv Where to write it

docs.title: run_contract
docs.text:
What happens when it runs? Runs the contract on a local CSV or Parquet file with Polars or DuckDB: how many rows pass, how many are quarantined, and each quarantine reason with its count. Nothing is written to the contract's target. Core does what the contract configures, including any notifications — see Safety and privacy.

Input Default path The contract file source The data file (CSV or Parquet) in the project engine polars polars or duckdb sample 10 How many example rows of each kind to return write_outputs false Save the good and quarantined rows under runs/

A typical sequence: generate_test_data → run_contract on the file it wrote.
